sources.title: EPA Cleaning sanitizing and disinfecting surfaces

steps.text: Confirm vendor business identity, authorized contact, service area, skills and availability.
Record insurer or broker verification of applicable insurance, policy dates and relevant exclusions. A certificate alone is not a coverage guarantee.
Confirm required licenses, worker classification review and site-specific qualifications before assignment. Unverified items block assignment.
Record acknowledgement of this exact SOP version and the job-specific safety instructions.
Confirm approved vendor terms and payment rules are on record; do not infer agreement from an application.
Confirm requester authority, property type, permitted areas, occupancy and service needs.
List included rooms/tasks, excluded work, surface sensitivities, access windows and measurable acceptance criteria.
Ask about known hazards, pets, sharps, bodily fluids, pests, damaged utilities and restricted equipment; route specialist work for review.
Record the client-approved scope, price, materials treatment, cancellation terms and revision before scheduling. No implied acceptance.
Match only verified vendors by service skill, coverage, service area and actual availability.
Confirm client and vendor acceptance of date, time zone, duration, scope and contact method.
Arrange access through restricted delivery. Do not put keys, lock codes or alarm codes in general notes or public links.
Assign escalation contact and review late arrival, unsafe conditions and access failure handling.
Record actual arrival and confirm correct site and authorized access.
Inspect assigned work areas with the client or authorized representative where possible. Record preexisting damage without declaring fault.
Capture only necessary, authorized condition photos. Avoid people, documents, valuables and access codes; use restricted job storage.
Check utilities, ventilation, trip/slip risks, equipment and required protective gear. Stop affected work when unsafe.
Escalate scope or condition differences before extra work; obtain an approved scope revision.
Read product labels and available safety data sheets; use only compatible products, protective equipment and ventilation specified for the task.
Never improvise chemical mixtures. Keep containers labelled and use products only as directed.
Separate restroom tools from kitchen and general-area tools. Keep clean supplies separate from soiled materials.
Work through the agreed area checklist; protect furnishings and manage wet floors with barriers or warnings.
If disinfection is in scope, use a suitable registered product and follow its surface, preparation and wet-contact-time directions. Do not promise sterilization.
Stop for unknown chemicals, sharps, suspected hazardous material, significant mold or unsafe equipment; isolate the area and contact the supervisor.
Replace approved linen and towels; separate soiled laundry and verify laundry scope.
Check agreed consumables and inventory; report missing or damaged items without charging anyone.
Check kitchen, bathroom, bedrooms and guest-touch surfaces against the approved list; report maintenance issues.
Confirm readiness against the next check-in deadline; do not mark available while safety or essential cleaning defects remain.
Confirm lawful access and vacancy status; never remove tenant belongings without documented authorization.
Complete scoped kitchen, bath, floors, fixtures and appliance surfaces using compatible methods.
Report leaks, electrical defects, pests and other maintenance issues separately; do not attempt unqualified repairs.
Confirm final area checklist and return access items through the approved custody process.
Respect occupied work areas, confidentiality and restricted rooms; do not open drawers or view documents.
Clean agreed touch points and shared facilities without damaging electronics.
Handle agreed ordinary waste only; report sharps, medical waste or unknown substances.
Check agreed closing tasks and lockup with authorized personnel; record exceptions without recording codes.
Agree a safe work zone and traffic separation with site management; stop if moving equipment enters the area.
Do not operate forklifts, production machinery or isolate energized equipment unless separately qualified and authorized.
Use methods compatible with the floor and approved contaminants; do not clean unidentified spills.
Have the site representative review barriers and safe reopening of completed areas.
Confirm written keep, move and dispose instructions; no independent disposal or appraisal of valuables.
Record delicate surfaces and existing damage; obtain permission before moving fragile objects.
Protect personal records, photographs and belongings; do not publish before-and-after images.
Reconcile moved items and exceptions with the authorized representative.
Follow the hotel room-status and entry procedure; respect do-not-disturb and guest privacy.
Use hotel-approved linen separation, replacement and lost-property procedures.
Complete property-specific room and bathroom quality checks; do not substitute this generic checklist for brand requirements.
Release room status only through the authorized supervisor after inspection.
Confirm trained operator, surface suitability, equipment condition, pedestrian exclusion and runoff plan before starting.
Never operate gasoline-powered equipment indoors or in enclosed spaces; keep exhaust away from doors, windows and air intakes.
Keep the spray away from people, animals and electrical equipment; do not inspect a leak with a hand.
Stop for injury or suspected injection wound and obtain urgent medical help; do not judge severity by skin appearance.
Review surface damage, debris and drainage; remove barriers only when the area is safe.
Inspect each scoped area against its acceptance criteria; record defects and exceptions.
Assign in-scope rework with an owner, due time and retest. Obtain approval for added scope rather than silently charging.
Confirm site safety, dry or clearly controlled floors, secure storage and removal of supplies.
Close defects only after verification. Unresolved defects remain visible at handover.
Record completed work, time, checklist version, deviations and restricted evidence references.
Request the authorized client representative’s explicit acceptance or list of issues; silence does not equal acceptance in this proposal.
Owner reviews completion and open incidents against approved terms. Crew checkbox alone does not authorize payment release.
Confirm approved split, fees, tax, materials and tips treatment for this job revision. Unknown terms block a payout plan.
Reconcile verified provider events, settled or available funds, refunds, disputes and prior payment references.
Check approved completion and dispute rules, then review a single idempotent payment plan. This SOP does not initiate a charge or transfer.
Record actual payment and payout outcomes separately; a transfer to a provider balance is not proof of bank receipt.
Check the agreed due date and actual provider status, including partial, failed or pending payment.
Prepare a factual reminder with invoice reference and approved payment route; review recipient and amount before sending.
Separate a disputed charge or disputed service from ordinary lateness; record the client response.
Review next service, payment plan or escalation under approved terms. Do not invent late fees, auto-debit, seize funds or initiate collections.
Stop affected work; protect people and prevent further damage only within safe training. For immediate danger call emergency services.
Record time, job, location, observations, parties and necessary evidence. Label allegations separately from verified facts.
Escalate promptly to the owner; prepare factual client and vendor communications for review, without admitting liability.
Preserve original evidence with restricted access and audit history; do not delete or edit originals to hide a defect.
Obtain vendor response, repair estimate and applicable insurer or broker guidance. Coverage, fault and deductions are not automatic.
Record approved resolution, responsible party, deadlines and verification; money actions require their separate authorization.

templates.title: Cancellation no show or access failure

steps.text: Record who reported the issue, scheduled time, contact attempt and actual access facts.
Offer only approved rescheduling or cancellation options; do not promise compensation or charge an unapproved fee.
Owner reviews contract terms, client notice and vendor commitments before a financial adjustment.
Store minimum necessary job evidence in restricted records, not public pages, message templates or source code.
Record return or approved disposal of temporary access material without copying its secret value into audit text.
Follow an owner-approved retention schedule and legal preservation instructions; do not delete evidence while a hold applies.
Record the requested change, reason, affected tasks and schedule impact without overwriting the accepted scope.
Obtain the owner and client acceptance of the revised scope and price before added work. Preserve both versions.
Confirm the assigned crew received the new checklist and can perform it safely.
Record the delay, absence or interruption and notify the dispatcher through the approved route.
Verify replacement crew skills, current eligibility and availability; do not bypass vetting to meet a deadline.
Confirm revised timing and any crew change with the client and replacement vendor.
Transfer only necessary job scope, completed steps and restricted access through approved channels. Preserve the original audit history.
Explain what location precision is used and who can see it. Availability is an explicit vendor choice, not an inference from location.
Record the vendor choice and policy version before any location-enabled discovery. Do not activate actual location collection through this checklist.
Provide an easy unavailable or revoke control; hide unavailable, stale or revoked entries from customer discovery.
Show only approved approximate discovery location publicly. Do not expose precise coordinates or retain a movement history by default.

review_required: Owner and vendor split and fee responsibility
Retention schedule and authorized evidence access
